Lifou|New Caledonia.f: Lifou is the largest Loyalty Island, a raised coral atoll covering 1,146 sq km.

Ouvéa|New Caledonia.f: Kanak independence militants killed four gendarmes and held 27 hostage in a cave on Ouvea in 1988.

Île des Pins|New Caledonia.f: More than 300 mysterious mounds of unknown origin dot the central plateau of the Isle of Pines.

Kaukura|Fr. Polynesia.f: Kaukura's lagoon covers 434 sq km, far more than its 13.5 sq km of land, and Roggeveen sighted it in 1722.

Takaroa|Fr. Polynesia.f: Dutch explorers Le Maire and Schouten reached Takaroa in April 1616 and named it Sondergrond Island.

Coron|Philippines.f: US carrier planes attacked up to 24 Japanese supply ships in Coron Bay on 24 Sept 1944, and the wrecks are now dive sites.

Maré|New Caledonia.f: Maré is a former coral atoll lifted about 120 meters, leaving fossil reef rock full of caves and pits.

Tioman|Malaysia.f: Tioman's reefs hold 350 species of hard coral from 67 genera, and its rainforest became a wildlife reserve in 1972.

Maupiti|Fr. Polynesia.f: Polynesian archaeological artifacts on Maupiti date back to at least AD 850.

Manihi|Fr. Polynesia.f: Manihi was the site of French Polynesia's first black pearl farm.

Takapoto|Fr. Polynesia.f: Roggeveen's flagship Afrikaansche Galey wrecked near Takapoto in 1722, and locals first learned of iron from its scraps.

Oksibil|Indonesia.f: Oksibil in Papua's highlands receives about 5,385 mm of rain a year.

Balimo|Papua New Guinea.f: Balimo sits on the Aramia River, one of only two river basins that are home to the Aramia snake-necked turtle.

Tiga|New Caledonia.f: A Kanak dance from tiny Tiga was sampled on Moby's 1999 album Play, and the island gave Ultraman Tiga its name.

Tanah Merah|Indonesia.f: Tanah Merah was built on the site of the Boven-Digoel camp, a Dutch political internment camp run from 1926 to 1943.
